t: Section 555 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:“(d) Any person who attempts or conspires to commit any offense under subsection (a) or subsection (c) of this section shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed for the offense, the commission of which was the object of the attempt or conspiracy.”.

fable.w: This section amends a criminal statute to extend penalties to attempts and conspiracies. It involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government. The only possible temptation is that it mentions 'any person,' but that person is a criminal defendant subject to penalties, not a participant in a federal decision.
fable.s: Any person who attempts or conspires to commit any offense under subsection (a) or subsection (c) of this section shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed for the offense

qwen_block.w: This section defines criminal penalties for attempt and conspiracy. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. It is purely a substantive criminal law provision.
qwen_block.s: Any person who attempts or conspires to commit any offense under subsection (a) or subsection (c) of this section shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed for the offense, the commission of which was the object of the attempt or conspiracy.

opus.w: This section only extends criminal penalties to people who attempt or conspire to commit offenses under 18 U.S.C. 555. It does not bring anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. Mentioning penalties and prosecution only describes criminal liability; it does not create a comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning:** One could read "subject to the same penalties" as involving the courts or other outside actors, since prosecution and sentencing come up. That reading doesn't hold. The section only sets criminal penalties for attempting or conspiring to commit an offense. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines criminal penalties for attempts or conspiracies to commit specific offenses. It does not involve the federal government consulting with, coordinating with, or granting decision-making input to any outside party. The mention of 'any person' refers to potential criminals, not participants in a governmental decision-making process. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Any person who attempts or conspires to commit any offense under subsection (a) or subsection (c) of this section shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed for the offense, the commission of which was the object of the attempt or conspiracy.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "any person" includes the general public, and thus involves outside parties. However, the definition of participation requires that the outside party be involved in a *federal decision* (e.g., consultation, advisory role, right to sue a decision). This section merely defines criminal penalties for attempts or conspiracies to commit offenses. It does not grant any procedural right to participate in government decision-making, nor does it require the government to consult with anyone. It is a substantive criminal law provision, not a procedural participation mechanism.
